title.text: Changeset review: making each change legible

n1.text:
What the feedback traced to

• "kept" = YOUR verdict (Keep), not the link. The op chip (add / + link) and the verdict chip sit side by side with no labels, so a new link reads "kept".
• "new source" = the link's SOURCE ELEMENT is new in this changeset. Nothing to do with source references — only 9 of 293 changes carry one.
• Product is spec layer 3, but the viewer knows 12 layers: 276 of 293 changes get a grey swatch.
• A link's inspector shows the sentence and the raw id only.
• "Links in this changeset" lists A predicate B with no direction, type or layer.
• Impact: ~280 nodes in 2 lanes, no search or filter.

n2.text:
Two vocabularies, two shapes

CHANGE (what the changeset does): solid tinted chip with a glyph — + element, + link, ~ update, − delete.

DECISION (what you said): outlined pill in its own labelled column — ✓ Keep, ✕ Drop, ? Ask, • Needs decision. Hidden in the inspector's related-links list once the changeset is applied.

n3.text:
Impact usability guidance

1. Start narrow: open on the changeset's own elements ("Changes only"), reach is opt-in via Follow.
2. Search jumps and focuses, it doesn't just highlight.
3. Filters are facets with counts: layer, change, element type, link category.
4. Big lanes collapse to a count + top types; expand on demand.
5. Focus = one element + its +1 layer; breadcrumb back to all.
6. Selection in the graph and the review list are the same selection.
